body.text: Fri, 11 Sept, 7:50 pm, Final score, Rabbitohs 10, Knights 20
NRL live: Nathan Cleary benched for Panthers-Knights preliminary final, Broncos beat Titans to reach NRL grand final
Nathan Cleary has been named on the bench for Penrith's preliminary final against the Newcastle Knights as the Panthers star struggles with a foot injury.
Meanwhile, train delays from Newcastle to Sydney have cause issues for travelling Knights fans.
Earlier, the Brisbane Broncos locked in an NRLW grand final rematch with the Sydney Roosters by taking down the Titans 20-8 on the Gold Coast.
Follow all the action in our live blog below, check out all the stats in the full NRL and NRLW ScoreCentres, and tune in to our live radio coverage.

16' It's firing up in the rain
Moses Leota drops the ball after a big tackle by Jermaine McEwen, who gets in the face of the Penrith prop.
Leota lets his frustration show and throws what I'll call a closed-fisted shove to the collarbone of McEwen, giving away a penalty as the teams come together.
15' Spectacular take and tumble by Talagi
My lord. Blaize Talagi has just taken one of the best and bravest catches I've ever seen, flying high over Greg Marzhew, who clips the Panther's legs and sends him flipping into the turf.
He smashes back to earth onto his back, but pops up and shapes to pass, just knocking on at the last moment as the defence arrives.
And the Panthers hit right back!
Isaah Yeo is orchestrating things in the middle and manipulating the defence.
Kalyn Ponga is caught up in the middle and the Panthers spin it right for Jack Cogger, who rolls a grubber into miles of space in behind and Blaize Talagi is all alone as he grounds it.
11' Talagi is whacked high
The Panthers get a set restart to help them into the red zone and they'll have a full set on the tryline as Bradman Best and Greg Marzhew hit Blaize Talagi high on a right side raid.
NEWCASTLE SCORES FROM 70 METRES OUT!!
The Knights run it on the fourth tackle and Bradman Best bursts through the attempted tackle of Blaize Talagi like he's not even there.
He comes to Dylan Edwards and has options inside and out. He perfectly sums it up to find Francis Manuleleua to dive over for the opener.
The noise as Best broke down the left was breathtaking and Silverchair is blaring out of the speakers for some extra Newcastle flavour.
One to watch: it sounded like Gerard Sutton warned Tom Jenkins for coming in with the knees as Manuleleua dove in, saying: "They've got a shot at goal, you don't want to give them another one."
4' Knights go for too much
Jack Cogger is smashed after kicking again, and this time Tyson Frizell was too late.
Gerard Sutton blows the penalty and Dylan Edwards kicks for goal from 18 metres in from touch to a chorus of jeers.
And he pushes the shot across the face! That's a huge miss and a signal that four points will not automatically become six as it often does when Cleary is kicking.
3' Cogger is obliterated
The first kick of the game sees Jack Cogger poke a high ball over to the right, and gets absolutely belted by Mat Croker as he does so.
All fair, all clean and all clear.
Cogger is back to his feet, but it would have been interesting to see if he stayed down, would Nathan Cleary be activated?
1' FRIZELL KNOCKS ON
The rain is falling and the field is slippery, and Knights forward Tyson Frizell knocks on in the first set to hand Penrith a golden opportunity from 40 metres out.
1' Penrith kicks off
And Tyson Frizell takes the first hit-up, sparking the "Newcastle" chants.
A moment's silence for fallen police officer
The stadium is silent for Constable Mia Lay.
The Knights run out to rapturous applause
The red and blue has taken over Homebush and the players are hearing it as they run out. You can see them soaking it up and loving it.
Then the bell tolls for the Panthers' arrival.
And they are every bit the villains for this crowd.
Newcastle's NRL grand final drought
The Knights don't have the longest NRL premiership drought but, at 25 years since their 2001 premiership, they have waited longer than any team to play in the decider.
Thank Joey for the 2023 NRLW premiership to keep the Novocastrians sated.
Broncos vs Roosters in the NRLW GF, as expected
The Titans had a brilliant season, including a 10-game winning streak, but ultimately the decider will be played between the two teams widely tipped at the start of the season.
Knights fans have taken over

Stadium Australia may as well be Little Newcastle at the moment. Knights fans have taken over the joint - the Novocastrians were given a rapturous reception when they hit the field for their warm up and Penrith were booed to within an inch of their lives.
Even with the train delays I think we're looking at a crowd of over 50,000 and most of them are red and blue.
Ivan Cleary on the decision to bench Nathan
Penrith coach Ivan Cleary isn't giving much away in terms of the decision to take Nathan Cleary out of the starting line-up.
"We just feel it gives us the best chance to navigate our way through the 80 minutes," he tells Fox.
"Just taking him out of the biggest impact at the start of the game."

Cleary admits his son and halfback has been limited over the past couple of weeks, but the flipside is getting to tell a "stoked" Jack Cole and Jack Cogger that they'll be starting a preliminary final.
No warm-ups for Nathan Cleary
We saw footage earlier of Nathan Cleary doing some foot exercises in the sheds while wearing sandshoes and now he's not out there warming up with the rest of the Panthers.
It will be fascinating to see how much they use him today.
What will the game plan be for Nathan Cleary?
Unless the Panthers are up by 24 points after 30 minutes, Nathan Cleary will surely be injected at some point in the first half, foot injury be damned.
The Panthers have embodied that "next man up" mentality and that will be embodied by Jacks Cole and Cogger in the halves to start this one.
But watch for Isaah Yeo to take a bigger role in the play-making through the middle early.
Fullback Dylan Edwards will also have increased responsibility, and he says the team has had two weeks to come up with a game plan around Cleary.
"We've known for a while," Edwards tells Fox.
"Once he gets on he field it's all systems go anyway."
Still, Penrith great Greg Alexander is adamant he will be on the field after 20 minutes.
"He'll be kicking," Alexander said on Fox Sports.
"He kicked at training on Thursday, he won't be goal-kicking."
Key Event
More on train delays for Newcastle Knights fans
Our Newcastle office is chatting to some of the Knights fans who are battling to get to Sydney for the preliminary final against the Penrith Panthers.
Cass Pascoe, who boarded the train at Broadmeadow just after 9am AEST, was stranded with other passengers for hours.
She said replacement buses and trains began to turn up shortly before 1pm.
Despite the extensive delays she said fellow Knights fans still remained positive they would make the game.
"The mood between passengers is still high and there's a big group chanting Newcastle," she said.
Pascoe said she eventually boarded a "very full" replacement train to Sydney's Central station.
Sydney Trains head of rail operations Jas Tumber said hundreds of passengers were impacted.
"We've got a train that has had to be terminated at Morisset that had approximately 300 passengers on there, which we've arranged eight replacement buses to come and pick up," he said.
"The key message for our passengers is to allow plenty of extra travel time if you are heading to the game.
"We absolutely apologise to all of those passengers and fans heading towards the [NRL] game."
Rail operations says technicians are onsite conducting repair work on the freight train that caused the delay.
There are 17 buses operating between Wyong and Hornsby, as well as trains running on either side of those stations.
Key Event
LATE MAIL: Nathan Cleary benched for Panthers-Knights prelim
Huge news from Homebush as the Penrith Panthers naming superstar halfback Nathan Cleary on the bench as he battles a foot complaint, described as a stress-related bone issue.
Also shifted from the starting line-up to the bench are Lindsay Smith and Isaiah Papali'i.
No changes to the Knights' 19.
